design.concept: A short two-step corridor for the company's manager. Step 1 welcomes them with what the platform already knows about the company, whether it is prepared, and what is still missing. Step 2 asks only for the missing mandatory data and holds the save and "see people" actions. Once the company is prepared, the screen points to the Studio.

views.purpose: Step 1: welcome card with the registered data (name, document, country, addresses, linked contacts), the "company prepared" indicator, the warning of what is missing, and the Studio guidance when ready. It has a single way forward.
Step 2 (with Back): form with only the missing data, the linked contacts shown read-only, the result of the save, and the actions to save and go to the organization's people.

design.decisions:
I followed the linearStepper template without inventing steps, because the contract has one command and no per-step commands. Step 1 is the opening and step 2 is the act that commits. There is no separate summary step because the company is redrawn by the shared after saving and step 1 becomes the confirmation. Each scene draws its own numbered rail with a fixed current step, so the rail is a map and never navigation and the page reads no scene state. Back is the scene host's own back control.

The fields shown follow the readonly missing-data field of the company, so the person is never asked again for what the platform has. The page only checks which of name, document, address or contact appears in it.

The address uses a two-row text field instead of the address-field molecule because the draft holds a plain list of address strings and the molecule's address event is not documented in the contract.

Loading, empty and error of the opening load are separate designed states. A missing-precondition error explains what is missing and offers a way back.

Save errors appear in body color above the buttons. Success appears in the same place as a polite status message. Save shows a running state while it commits.
